$comment: Native (.so) binary hardening weaknesses. These are build-time exploit mitigations that are either present or forgotten; the nativelib worker reads the ELF headers and the adapter turns the absence of a mitigation into one of these. Severities are deliberately conservative: a missing mitigation is not itself a vulnerability, it is a weakened defence that makes an unrelated memory bug more exploitable, so these confirm and rank rather than accuse. maswe_id stays null for the same reason as the rest of the pack: unverified from here.

weaknesses.title: Native library has an executable stack
weaknesses.description: A shared object marks its stack executable (a writable and executable GNU_STACK segment). This removes one of the oldest exploit mitigations: with a writable, executable stack, data an attacker controls on the stack can be run as code, which turns a stack buffer overflow directly into code execution.
weaknesses.remediation: Rebuild the library without an executable stack. This is almost always an accident from hand-written assembly or an old toolchain; add '.section .note.GNU-stack' to assembly sources or pass -Wl,-z,noexecstack at link time.

weaknesses.title: Native library has no RELRO
weaknesses.description: The library has no GNU_RELRO segment, so its Global Offset Table stays writable after loading. An attacker with an arbitrary write can redirect a GOT entry to hijack control flow. Full RELRO (RELRO plus eager binding) marks the GOT read-only once relocations are done and closes that technique.
weaknesses.remediation: Link with -Wl,-z,relro,-z,now for full RELRO. The NDK enables this by default, so its absence usually points at a custom or outdated build.

weaknesses.title: Native library shows no stack-protector symbols
weaknesses.description: No stack-protector symbols (__stack_chk_fail) were found in the library, which suggests it was compiled without stack canaries. Canaries detect a classic stack buffer overflow before the overwritten return address is used. This is reported at INFO because a library with no vulnerable functions legitimately carries no canary, so it is a prompt to check the build flags rather than a defect on its own.
weaknesses.remediation: Build with -fstack-protector-strong. The NDK sets this by default; its absence usually means a custom toolchain or explicit opt-out.
